title: Hilary Swank Announces Pregnancy at 52: Expecting Third Child, CBS News Reports
body:
Hollywood’s beloved Oscar‑winner Hilary Swank has once again captured headlines, this time for a deeply personal milestone rather than a screen role. In a heartfelt Instagram post shared on Tuesday, the 52‑year‑old actress revealed that she is expecting her third child, due in December. The news follows Swank’s earlier announcement that she gave birth to twins—a boy and a girl—in 2022 when she was 48, marking one of the most high‑profile later‑in‑life pregnancies in recent memory. Fans and fellow celebrities flooded the actress’s social media with congratulations, underscoring both admiration for her continued vitality and a broader cultural conversation about motherhood at an older age.

Swank’s journey to motherhood has been anything but conventional. After a celebrated early career that included two Academy Awards for “Boys Don’t Cry” (1999) and “Million Dollar Baby” (2004), she stepped back from the limelight to focus on family life. In 2018, she married actor and producer Philip White, and the couple welcomed their first child, a son named Calvin, in 2020. The arrival of twins—Sasha and Samuel—four years later positioned Swank among a growing cohort of women who are choosing to start or expand families well into their late 40s and early 50s, a demographic shift made possible by advances in reproductive technology and changing societal expectations.

Medical experts note that while pregnancies after 50 are still relatively rare, they are becoming more common thanks to in‑vitro fertilization (IVF) and egg‑donor programs. The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists emphasizes that older mothers typically require more intensive prenatal monitoring to manage risks such as gestational diabetes, hypertension, and pre‑term birth. Swank has not disclosed the specifics of her fertility treatment, but her openness about the timeline may help destigmatize discussions around assisted reproduction, especially for women in the public eye who often face scrutiny over personal choices.

Beyond the medical dimensions, Swank’s announcement resonates culturally. In an industry where youth has long been prized, her continued prominence challenges entrenched ageist narratives. Her willingness to share the joys and challenges of late‑stage motherhood aligns with a broader movement of high‑profile figures—such as actress Jane Fonda, who welcomed a child at 55, and former First Lady Michelle Obama, who has spoken candidly about parenting older children—who are redefining what “family planning” looks like in the 21st century. Social media reactions have highlighted both admiration for Swank’s resilience and a growing acceptance that parenthood does not adhere to a single timeline.

The actress also used the platform to reflect on the emotional landscape of her expanding family. In the caption accompanying a photo of herself cradling her newborn twins, Swank wrote, “Our family is growing, our love is expanding, and we can’t wait to meet the newest member of our tribe.” The sentiment underscores a narrative that many new parents echo: the profound sense of purpose and fulfillment that accompanies each addition, irrespective of age. Moreover, Swank’s candidness may inspire other women who have postponed childbearing for career or personal reasons, reassuring them that options remain viable later in life.

Looking ahead, Swank’s upcoming due date in December places her pregnancy squarely in the holiday season, a time traditionally associated with family gatherings and celebrations. While the actress has not announced any professional projects slated for 2024, her continued involvement in selective film and television roles suggests she may return to the screen after maternity leave, potentially bringing a fresh perspective shaped by her evolving personal experiences. As the entertainment world watches, Swank’s story will likely continue to spark dialogue about the intersection of fame, fertility, and the evolving definition of motherhood in contemporary society.
